name: Non-standard ERC-20 behaviour: fee-on-transfer, rebase, hooks, missing return
requires: a token the protocol integrates, whose transfer semantics may differ from the standard
protocol accounting that assumes received == sent
a deposit, repay, or collateral path using that token
questions: Does the protocol credit the requested amount or the measured balance delta after transfer?
Is the token fee-on-transfer, and does the fee apply on transferFrom as well?
Does the token rebase, so a stored balance drifts from the real one?
Does transfer/transferFrom return bool, or return nothing (USDT-style)?
Is the integration using safeTransfer, or a raw transfer whose return is unchecked?
Does the token have a transfer hook (ERC777, ERC1363) that can reenter?
Is the token blocklist/blacklist capable, so a transfer can revert and strand funds?
Does the protocol hold the token balance and compute shares from address(this).balance?
false_positives: The protocol measures the balance delta, which is correct for all of these
The token is a known-standard immutable with no fee and no hook
safeTransfer is used everywhere, so a missing return cannot silently pass
The rebase is positive-only and the protocol only ever reads its own ledger
poc_must_show: a deposit where credited amount and received amount are both printed and differ
the resulting position or share count that is now wrong
a control run with a standard token at the same amount
the eventual loss or insolvency path, quantified
impact_bar: Reportable when the mismatch creates a withdrawable amount exceeding what was deposited, or strands funds, quantified per token. Informational for a token the protocol does not actually integrate.
